issues.legal_issue: A tank dedicated to receive an inam for its repair can qualify as a charitable institution, so property in an abolished inam dedicated to the tank is registered for the tank rather than in the name of its manager.
material_facts: The inam register recorded the grant as being to the tank and for repairing it, and stated that the grant would continue while repairs were performed.
The register identified the appellant’s ancestor as manager of the charitable institution, and the appellant was managing the tank at the time of the dispute.
The register described the tank as useful to the village’s people and cattle, and recorded that the inam’s proceeds had been redirected to a replacement tank at the villagers’ request.
The authorities found that the grant was in favour of the tank, rather than a grant to the appellant’s family subject to a repair obligation.
issues.conclusion: The tank was a charitable institution within section 2(E) of the Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1956. The inam property was to be registered in the name of the tank and managed by its manager; the appellant was to continue managing it for as long as he remained manager.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, a tank may be an object of charity, and a dedication in its favour may constitute a charitable institution. Whether something is an institution depends on the context in which the term is used; an institution may require human management without it being necessary to decide whether it has separate juristic personality. Applying section 2(E) of the Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1956, the Court relied on Minister of National Revenue v. Trusts and Guarantee Co. Ltd. on the contextual meaning of “institution”; Masjid Shahid Ganj v. Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee on institutions and management; Jamnabai v. Khimji Vallubdass on the charitable character of public water works; and V. Mariyappa v. B.K. Puttaramayya on tanks maintained as public institutions under Hindu law.

rule.if: inam_abolition_registration_proceeding and grant_dedicated_to_tank and tank_served_public_use and tank_manager_identified

predicates.inam_abolition_registration_proceeding: The dispute concerns registration of property after an inam has been abolished.
predicates.grant_dedicated_to_tank: The grant was made in favour of the tank, rather than to an individual or family subject to a duty to repair it.
predicates.tank_served_public_use: The tank was maintained for the use or benefit of the public or community.
predicates.tank_manager_identified: A person was identified as the manager responsible for managing the tank.

issues.definition: When a registration dispute follows abolition of an inam dedicated to a tank serving public use and the tank has an identified manager, the property is registered in the tank’s name and managed by that manager.
